clauses.requirement: Annex 7 para 4.3 (test requirements): Radiated emission measurements on the ESA (rear lamp electronics) shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver using the parameters defined in Table 1 and Table 2; spectrum analysers and FFT-based instruments meeting CISPR 16-1-1 may be used for conformity measurements; FFT-based instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time, with a minimum measurement time of 1 s per analysis frequency band (real-time mode).

Table 1 spectrum analyser parameters for 30 to 1,000 MHz: peak detector RBW at -3 dB of 100/120 kHz with minimum scan time 100 ms/MHz; quasi-peak detector RBW at -6 dB of 120 kHz with minimum scan time 20 s/MHz; if a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).

Table 2 scanning receiver parameters for 30 to 1,000 MHz: peak detector BW at -6 dB 120 kHz, maximum step size 60 kHz, minimum dwell time 5 ms; quasi-peak detector BW at -6 dB 120 kHz, maximum step size 60 kHz, minimum dwell time 1 s; for purely broadband disturbances the maximum frequency step size may be increased up to a value not greater than the bandwidth value; for emissions from brush commutator motors without an electronic control unit the maximum step size may be increased up to five times the bandwidth.

Annex 7 para 4.4 Measurements: unless otherwise specified, the configuration with the LV harness closer to the antenna shall be tested; the antenna phase centre shall be in line with the centre of the longitudinal part of the wiring harnesses for frequencies up to 1,000 MHz; the Technical Service shall test at the intervals specified in CISPR 12 across 30 to 1,000 MHz; alternatively, if the manufacturer provides whole-band measurement data from an ISO 17025 accredited laboratory recognized by the Type Approval Authority, the Technical Service may divide the range into 14 bands (30-34, 34-45, 45-60, 60-80, 80-100, 100-130, 130-170, 170-225, 225-300, 300-400, 400-525, 525-700, 700-850, 850-1,000 MHz) and test at the 14 frequencies with highest emission in each band to confirm the ESA meets the Annex requirements; if the limit is exceeded, investigations shall ensure this is due to the ESA and not background radiation.

Annex 7 para 4.5 Readings: the maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.

Figure 1 Open area test site: the test shall be set up on an open area test site with the electrical/electronic sub-assembly test area boundary defined and a level clear area free from electromagnetic reflecting surfaces.

Figure 2 test configuration for ESAs involved in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid (example for biconical antenna, dimensions in mm): the setup shall comprise the keyed items, including RF absorber material, ESA (grounded locally if required by test plan), LV test harness, LV load simulator (placement and ground connection per CISPR 25 clause 6.4.2.5), power supply, LV artificial network, ground plane bonded to shielded enclosure, low relative permittivity support (εr ≤ 1.4), biconical antenna, double-shielded 50 Ω coaxial cable, bulkhead connector, measuring instrument, stimulation and monitoring system, HV harness, HV load simulator, HV AN, HV power supply, HV feed-through, AC/DC charger harness, AC/DC load simulator (e.g. PLC), AMN(s) or DC-charging-AN(s), AC/DC power supply and AC/DC feed-through; applicable only where the ESA is involved in such charging mode.

Annex 8: the method of measurement of radiated narrowband electromagnetic emissions from electrical/electronic sub-assemblies (ESAs), such as the LED electronics of the rear lamp, shall be applied as specified in this Annex.
